businessProblem: Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services Ltd. (IL&FS) and its group companies have experienced active defaults on multiple debt instruments in August and September 2018, including term deposits, commercial paper, NCDs, inter-corporate deposits, and other obligations. The defaults have triggered rating downgrades across group instruments and are causing visible systemic contagion across Indian money markets, mutual funds, debt markets, and equity markets. The group's business model — financing long-gestation infrastructure projects through a complex network of subsidiaries and SPVs using short- and medium-term debt — has produced a structural asset-liability mismatch that cannot be resolved through normal cash management. Group-level debt and obligations are not transparently visible. Governance and risk oversight have failed to prevent the structural accumulation of liquidity risk. Emergency intervention is required to contain cascading defaults and systemic contagion before the crisis becomes uncontrollable.

evidence.finding: Active defaults on term deposits, short-term deposits, inter-corporate deposits, commercial paper, NCDs, and other debt instruments across IL&FS Group companies in August and September 2018

Structural asset-liability mismatch: long-dated infrastructure project cash flows are being funded by short- and medium-term debt instruments, creating repayment obligations that project revenues cannot service on schedule
Multiple credit rating agencies have downgraded IL&FS instruments to below investment grade following the defaults; this has triggered forced selling and redemption pressure
Group-level debt is distributed across a complex structure of subsidiaries and SPVs; the true aggregate debt position and cross-entity obligations are not transparently visible
Defaults and rating downgrades are causing active contagion across Indian money markets, mutual fund redemption pressure, debt market stress, and equity market adverse effects
Confidence in the broader NBFC sector is deteriorating as a result of IL&FS defaults; systemic risk extends beyond the group itself
Board and management governance framework has failed to identify and address the structural liquidity and asset-liability mismatch before defaults occurred
Infrastructure project financing model involves long gestation periods and hundreds of subsidiaries/SPVs; operational complexity has made risk aggregation and cash management extremely difficult

clientContext.size: Large systemically significant Indian NBFC and infrastructure group; several hundred subsidiaries and SPVs across infrastructure segments
clientContext.revenueImpactUrgency: CRITICAL — active defaults and systemic market contagion in progress; each day without intervention increases cascading default risk and systemic damage

ownerConstraintProfile.bottleneckRisk: VERY HIGH — existing management and board have demonstrated inability to prevent structural liquidity failure; decision-making capability is severely compromised
ownerConstraintProfile.followThroughRisk: VERY HIGH — no voluntary corrective action has been initiated despite defaults being active; follow-through on restructuring requires external authority
ownerConstraintProfile.resistanceToChange: HIGH — complex organisational structure and long-standing business model create structural inertia; voluntary asset monetisation and restructuring are unlikely at adequate pace without external governance
ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: CRITICALLY IMPAIRED — management has failed to address structural asset-liability mismatch before crisis; independent crisis governance is required
